Agent platform eval

This report is a controls comparison of two ways to run Claude Code on an issue. The experiment ran to settle the direction of dotnet-software-factory v2.

Source: the repo. Design and status: the plan.

How to read it

Cloud Sessions is a VM that Anthropic manages. The platform is the factory at v1.1.0 in Docker, on a self-hosted runner in a lab VM. Both arms ran the same agent on the same model, claude-sonnet-5-5. They ran against one target repo, sbiondolillo/platform-eval-sample. Issue #1 is the delivery, and issue #2 is the probes.

A probe run in the real product proves every Cloud cell. A public asset proves every platform cell. Each cell links its proof.

The controls

rowCloud SessionsPlatform
cloud-logging Cloud Sessions keep the error text in the server-side transcript, readable by signed-in accounts through the web UI, the Share link and the CLI; nothing is exported to disk. the GitHub job log holds the 403 line and the stack trace for 90 days, readable by any signed-in GitHub account, and the gateway ledger holds the run's calls and spend but not the failure.
substrate the agent runs as root with cap_sys_admin inside its own Firecracker microVM, so the VM boundary is the whole isolation. the agent runs as an unprivileged uid with Docker's default capabilities in a container that shares the runner VM's kernel, so the container and the VM are two boundaries, and the factory sets none of the container's confinement itself.
model-credential the VM holds the account's OAuth token in a file that the root agent can read, and model calls skip the egress proxy, so the credential that the agent can read has the reach of the whole account. the container holds only a lab gateway key, usable from inside the lab and logged per call, and the vendor key never enters the Sandbox VLAN, but the gateway sets no budget or model list on that key.
forge-credential the sandbox holds no token on disk, but the managed proxy injects the operator's own account credential with admin on the one granted repo, scoped away from the owner's other repos until add_repo is called. the agent's container holds no forge credential at all; the operator's fine-grained PAT and a job-scoped Actions token both sit in the factory process on the host, and the pull request is opened under the operator account.
vault-secret the managed proxy attaches the secret on the way out and only to its allowed hosts, so the agent's VM never holds a value it can read. infisical run puts the secret in the runner job's environment, so the factory process can read it and must attach it itself, and the agent's container gets it only when the factory passes it by name.
egress a local relay tunnels HTTPS only to exact allowed hostnames on port 443, and the gateway intercepts every direct port 443 connection and answers it itself, so no request reaches the internet except through the relay. Squid tunnels only to the hosts on the runner's per-source allowlist, which the operator edits by hand, and the firewall drops every direct connection, so Squid is the only path out.
tool-model-policy the operator picks any of twelve models with no control and the account's connectors set the tools, so the only controls observed were the egress relay, the start-time tool loading and a model-side safeguard that acts on prompt content. the factory fixes the model and the tools in code and Squid stops a new remote server, but the agent holds a gateway key with no model list and runs with every tool allowed, so it can call any gateway model on its own.
run-history sessions are listed and read only inside the product, in the web UI, the Share link, claude --teleport and the in-session MCP tools, and no documented API or CLI command lists them or exports a transcript to a file. gh lists the runs and downloads the 90-day job log, the gateway ledger holds every model call, and the model transcripts are files that the v1.2.1 starter pushes to a private store repo, but this target repo's v1.1.0 workflow has no store step, so they stay on the runner host only until the next run.
spend-attribution the documented environment route exported nothing in four sessions, the Claude Code process held none of the variables, and spend is read only from Anthropic's usage view. with a nine-name pass-through in the factory, the cost metric and one event per API request land in the operator's Grafana keyed by session id, and the metric reads within one export interval of the factory's own log.
audit-record the in-VM transcript is root-writable and only the auto-mode classifier stopped an append and a delete, so the record a compromised agent cannot erase is the server-side transcript outside the VM. the agent can edit or delete its own transcript on the runner with no control, so the records it cannot erase are the host-written job log, pull request history and the gateway's per-call ledger.
github-start a label can start a Cloud session, but only through a GitHub job that the repo owner writes and that holds a per-task bearer token, and the session's reply stays at claude.ai/code unless the prompt posts it back. the factory label starts the delivery run on the self-hosted runner directly through the workflow's issues: labeled trigger, gated to the repo owner, with no start credential.
crash-resume the Stop button loses nothing, and an idle reclaim keeps the disk and the history and kills every process, so a session resumes on its own files. a factory job has no resume; the container is removed at job end and only the pushed branch, the pull request and the saved transcript remain.
subagent-record the subagent keeps its own transcript in the VM's session folder, and the server-side transcript keeps its report and a row with its model, but whether the subagent's own transcript outlives the container is pending the reclaim step. the subagent's transcript lands beside the parent's on the runner host until the next job, it is never uploaded without the v1.2.1 store step, and the gateway ledger counts its calls under dsf with no link to the parent.
toolchain a setup script in the environment installs the SDK once, and later sessions start from a filesystem snapshot that the docs say is rebuilt on a script or allowlist change and after about seven days, but the UI shows no setup duration. the factory builds a 2.11 GB image from its own Dockerfile on the runner host at first use in about 66 s, each job then pays about 16 s of toolchain setup, and the image never expires and changes only when someone deletes it.
branch-protection the session pushed to protected main and the push landed as an administrator bypass, because the proxy pushes as the operator's admin account and the protection lets administrators bypass, so the protection does not bind the agent. the factory's source pushes only its own branch and opens a pull request, so the required checks apply at the merge, but the PAT is on the same admin account and the protection would not stop a direct push.
setup-cost Cloud Sessions took 25 operator steps and 4 secrets, all in web forms, GitHub and the workstation, with 8 steps and no secret to reach the first pull request and no lab host touched. the platform took 28 operator steps and no new secret in the experiment, on top of 9 lab items and 4 secrets that the lab already held, and it touched 3 lab hosts in the experiment and 6 with its prerequisites.

The conditional

A verdict hides the rows that are the same under either choice. Read the conditional cell by cell.

Rows Cloud Sessions covers today

  • cloud-logging: the server-side transcript keeps the error text for signed-in accounts.
  • substrate: each session runs in its own Firecracker microVM.
  • vault-secret: the managed proxy attaches the secret on the way out, so the VM never holds a value it can read.
  • egress: a local relay tunnels HTTPS only to exact allowed hostnames. The platform covers this row too, with a hand-edited allowlist.
  • audit-record: the server-side transcript outside the VM is a record that a compromised agent cannot erase.
  • github-start: a label can start a Cloud session, through a glue job that the repo owner writes.
  • crash-resume: an idle reclaim keeps the disk and the history, so a session resumes on its own files.
  • toolchain: a setup script installs the SDK once, and later sessions start from a filesystem snapshot.

Rows the factory owner must build under either choice

Both arms act under the operator's admin account. So a non-admin identity and a protection with no bypass are build items, whichever arm wins.

  • forge-credential: the Cloud proxy injects the operator's own admin credential, and the platform's PAT is on the same admin account.
  • branch-protection: the Cloud session pushed to protected main as an admin bypass, and the protection would not stop a direct push from the platform's PAT.

Rows only the platform can hold

  • model-credential: on Cloud Sessions the agent can read the account's OAuth token. The platform container holds only a gateway key, and the platform owes a budget on that key.
  • tool-model-policy: on Cloud Sessions the operator picks any of twelve models with no control. The platform fixes the model in code, and owes a model list on the gateway key.

Rows the docs do not settle, with the probe result

  • run-history: no documented API or CLI command lists Cloud sessions or exports a transcript.
  • spend-attribution: the documented environment route exported nothing in four Cloud sessions. The platform lands the cost metric with a nine-name pass-through.
  • subagent-record: whether the subagent's own transcript outlives the container is pending the reclaim step.

setup-cost: Cloud Sessions took 25 operator steps and 4 secrets. The platform took 28 steps and no new secret, on top of 9 lab items and 4 secrets that the lab already held.

One rung per arm

A trust ladder grades the phases of one change: issue, plan, build, review, feedback, deliver and merge. Each rung up hands one phase from a person to an agent or to code.

  • Rung 0: every phase is a person.
  • Rung 1: plan and build are an agent. Review is an agent plus a person. Deliver is code.
  • Rung 2: feedback is an agent that answers its own review threads.
  • Rung 3: the issue is an agent.
  • Rung 4: the review loses its person.
  • Rung 5: merge is code.

Two lines hold at every rung. Deliver is code. The agent never holds the credential that opens the pull request.

Platform: rung 2

The factory's source pushes the branch and opens the pull request. The agent's container holds no forge credential. The review is an agent gate, with a person at the merge.

Proof: forge-credential, platform-delivery.

Cloud Sessions: below rung 1

The agent itself pushed the branch and opened PR 5. It did this through the managed proxy, with the operator's admin credential. In the branch-protection probe, it pushed to protected main. Deliver is the agent, not code.

Rung 1 needs a deliver step outside the session and a non-admin identity. The glue job from the github-start row is the place to build it.

Proof: forge-credential, branch-protection, github-start.

2026-10-25. Every cell links its proof. A cell with no public proof says so.
